title: Lead generation for IT services: How to find companies with active projects
summary: Improve lead generation for IT services. Find active projects, check supplier needs and reach buyers with practical outreach examples.
body_markdown:
A cloud migration announcement can look like a reason to contact a company. But if the full announcement names an implementation partner, the work your team hoped to pitch may already be covered.


Lead generation for IT services means finding organizations with a relevant technical need and a realistic path to a sales conversation. If you run an IT consultancy, development agency or managed service provider, you need to understand the work and who owns it. You also need to check whether an external supplier could still participate.


Referrals, service pages, content and outbound can all help generate leads. Here, we’ll focus on project-led prospecting: using evidence of current or planned work to decide which accounts to research and approach.


## Start with the IT project your team can deliver


“Companies that need IT support” is too broad to be a useful targeting brief. A business looking for overnight help desk coverage has different requirements from one replacing its finance system.


Before researching accounts, define the work you can take on. Specify the platforms you support and the conditions you need to deliver the project.


Your service Project situation to investigate Important fit check


Cloud migration consulting A company planning to move specified workloads Platform, workload complexity and internal delivery capability


ERP or CRM implementation A business selecting, replacing or extending a system Product expertise, implementation scope and supplier selection stage


Managed IT services An organization reviewing support arrangements or adding locations Coverage, geography, service requirements and existing contracts


Software development and integration A company planning an application or connecting systems Technical scope, ownership and whether external development is being considered


Use these situations as research leads. A business opening an office, for example, may have no plans to change its managed service provider.


Include exclusions in the account brief, too. Be clear if your team supports only one cloud platform, needs local delivery access or cannot take on a large integration programme.


An[ideal customer profile template](https://blog.floworks.ai/ideal-customer-profile-template/) can help document the company criteria. Add the project requirements alongside them so researchers can assess both customer fit and delivery fit.


## Where to find evidence of an IT project


Look for descriptions of work a company is considering or carrying out. Save the original source and its date so a colleague can check why you selected the account.


### Supplier invitations and procurement notices


An invitation to propose services gives you a clearer route to a buyer than a general growth announcement. Before adding it to your pipeline, read the scope and deadline, along with the participation requirements and instructions for contacting the buyer.


For firms pursuing US federal work,[SAM.gov Contract Opportunities](https://sam.gov/opportunities) provides a public search. Its records include pre-solicitation, solicitation, award and sole-source notices. Anyone can search; an account enables saved searches and following changes.


Check the notice type before acting. An award notice can confirm that a supplier has already been selected, so it is not an invitation to compete for the same work.


Public-sector procurement is an option if your services and qualifications fit its requirements. Private companies may publish supplier requests on their own websites or use a separate procurement portal.


### Company announcements and published plans


Company newsrooms, investor updates and published technology plans can describe migrations, system replacements or integration programmes.


Read the full announcement for details such as the platform, delivery date and responsible team. Note any appointed partner and check whether the work is planned, underway or complete.


Try narrowing your searches to a service and evidence that a company is considering suppliers. For example:


> “cloud migration” “seeking a partner” manufacturing


> “ERP implementation” “request for proposal”


Results from these example searches still need checking. Open the original document to verify whether the opportunity is available.


### Project-specific vacancies


A vacancy may describe responsibilities such as migrating applications, coordinating an ERP rollout or integrating systems after an acquisition.


Those responsibilities can help you identify a project, though the company may be hiring to deliver the entire programme internally. The vacancy alone cannot tell you whether any work will be outsourced.


Use the responsibilities to assess whether there is a defined part of the project your service could support. A generic technology keyword in the skills list gives you much less to work with.


### Expansion, acquisitions and existing relationships


An acquisition or new location can justify investigating integration, infrastructure or support needs. First establish what the company has actually said about its plans.


A customer or partner introduction may provide more direct context. Ask which team owns the work and what kind of help is being considered. An introduction alone does not confirm a funded project.


Evidence found What it can establish What still needs checking


Open supplier invitation A stated requirement and submission route Current status, eligibility, scope and deadline


First-party project announcement An initiative the company has publicly described Current phase and whether a partner is already appointed


Project-specific vacancy Responsibilities the employer wants someone to perform Internal delivery plans and any external support requirement


Acquisition or site expansion A business change Whether a relevant IT project follows from it


Customer or partner introduction A route to a conversation The contact’s involvement, need and next step


## Check whether the project is still open to an external partner


Even when a project fits your technical expertise, the company may have no reason to evaluate another supplier. Check both fit and availability before approaching it.


Use the evidence to answer as much as you can:


- What work is actually described?
- Which phase is it in?
- Does the scope fit our capabilities?
- Has a supplier already been selected?
- Is there a stated route for considering external help?
- Which important details remain unknown?


Record what you still don’t know. Write “Budget not confirmed” when you have no evidence of a project value.


Microsoft’s[migration planning guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/migrate/plan-migration) separates readiness, team skills, workload sequencing and stakeholder involvement. It also discusses bringing in external expertise when a team lacks experience. A cloud consultancy can use these topics to qualify an account, though a public migration announcement will leave some questions unanswered.


### Use project stage to decide the next action


Project stage Example evidence Appropriate next action


Possible need Expansion announcement with no IT scope Research further before making a project claim


Planned initiative Company describes a future migration or replacement Check ownership, scope and how delivery will be resourced


Supplier evaluation Current invitation for relevant services Review requirements and follow the stated process


Delivery underway Implementation has started or a partner is named Check for explicitly unassigned work; avoid pitching an already-awarded scope


Completed project Go-live announcement or retrospective case study Exclude from the original project campaign; investigate later needs only if there is evidence


Check the project dates even if the page was published recently. Record the publication date, any project dates mentioned and the date you checked the source. Flag any uncertainty about whether the work is still current.


## A worked example: qualifying a cloud migration account


Consider a hypothetical consultancy that assesses and migrates business applications to Azure. It serves manufacturers and can handle application dependencies and migration planning.


A researcher finds a manufacturer’s announcement describing a planned migration, plus an infrastructure vacancy mentioning responsibility for the programme. This gives the consultancy an account to investigate, with several questions still open. The researcher records the findings:


Question Current finding


Is there a relevant project? The company has publicly described a migration


Does the technology fit? Azure is named, matching the consultancy’s expertise


Who appears involved? The infrastructure team has a role in the programme


Is external support required? Unknown


Has a partner been appointed? Not established from the sources reviewed


What should happen next? Check for supplier announcements and identify the project owner


Suppose further research reveals that a partner has already been appointed for the full migration. The consultancy should remove the account from this campaign unless there is separate evidence of work still available.


If supplier arrangements remain unclear, the researcher could ask the appropriate owner a short question based on the facts found so far.


An illustrative message, not one sent to a real prospect:


> Your company’s update describes a planned Azure migration. Our team helps manufacturers assess application dependencies before moving workloads. Is migration assessment already covered by your internal team or an appointed partner, or are you considering external support?


A reply that the work is fully covered answers the qualification question, even if it produces no meeting.


## Turn project research into a useful sales conversation


### Find the person responsible for the work


For a cloud migration, an infrastructure leader or programme owner may be a useful starting point. An ERP implementation may involve the application owner and finance operations. Managed services can involve IT operations and procurement.


These are roles to investigate. Check each person’s current responsibilities; the most senior technology title may not own the decision.


If the company has a formal supplier process, follow its designated contact and submission route when researching people to approach.


### Offer help with a defined decision


Offer help that fits the project stage and your team’s capabilities. A migration readiness assessment may be appropriate, or the buyer may need an integration scoping session or a discussion about support coverage.


Be specific about what the buyer will receive. Define the scope and output of a migration assessment, for example. If you’re offering a general product demonstration, describe it that way so the buyer can distinguish it from an independent technical assessment.


Link to the relevant service page on your website. If you have a comparable customer example, include it too. Check that it matches the technical problem and delivery scope; a shared industry alone may not make it relevant.


### Keep a record that another seller can use


Add these fields to your[B2B prospect list](https://blog.floworks.ai/how-to-build-a-prospect-list/) :


Field What to record


Account and relevant service The company and the specific engagement being considered


Source evidence Original URLs, publication dates and dates checked


Project scope and stage The work described and its current phase


Technical and delivery fit Supported platforms, location, capacity and exclusions


Supplier status Open evaluation, named partner or unconfirmed


Project owner Current contact and evidence of relevant responsibilities


Unanswered questions Missing scope, timing, budget or buying-process details


Next action and owner Who will investigate, contact, submit or close the record


Pass these details to sales with the account so the seller can see why it was selected and what still needs confirmation.


### Measure whether the research produces relevant opportunities


Review how many researched accounts have credible project evidence, how many conversations confirm a need for external support and how many progress to an agreed sales opportunity.


Record exclusions, too. Knowing whether accounts were rejected because the work was already awarded, the technology was unsupported or the delivery requirements were unsuitable helps you identify targeting problems.


Keep accounts with publicly described projects as research candidates until they meet your team’s agreed opportunity criteria. Only then should they enter qualified pipeline.

## Frequently asked questions


### How do IT services companies generate leads?


IT services firms can use referrals, partnerships, service-focused content, search campaigns and outbound research. For project-led prospecting, start with a defined service, find relevant project evidence and check whether the company could still consider an external supplier.


### Does a job posting mean a company needs an IT services provider?


No. It may describe a relevant initiative, but the employer could be hiring people to deliver the work internally. Check the responsibilities, corroborate the project and ask how external support is being considered.


### How can I tell whether an IT project is still available?


Check the latest source documents, project dates, supplier announcements and procurement status. If those sources do not establish the position, ask the designated project or procurement contact. Treat availability as unconfirmed until you have supporting evidence.
